messages:
alex: quick check — after the canary deploy last night I want a one-line pointer to the SM% + KV cache hit + memory panels for pool-42. Trying to assemble a short snapshot for the oncall handoff. can anyone paste the direct panel links?

maya: sure — Grafana panels are under 'runtime/gpu-capacity'. for pool-42 filters use "pool=pool-42" in the dashboard var. panels: SM% (panel 21), KV hit rate (panel 37), GPU memory (panel 12). link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/runtime/gpu-capacity?orgId=1&var-pool=pool-42 :point_right:

chen: pinging some quick context: the canary had slightly higher SM% but lower KV hit (around 62%) which pushed batch sizes to fall back. saw a few small evictions (~3/min) at ~02:15 UTC. nothing catastrophic but explains the 20% latency bump on short requests.

sam: if people want prom queries:
```
# avg SM utilization per GPU over 5m
avg by (gpu) (rate(gpu_sm_active_cycles_total[5m]) / rate(gpu_cycles_total[5m]) * 100)
# kv cache hit rate for pool-42
sum(kv_cache_hits{pool="pool-42"}) / sum(kv_cache_lookups{pool="pool-42"})
```

irene: re: alerts — current kv-hit alert is at <60% (3m for 5m). given last night's baseline i suggest lowering to 55% for the shared pools and add a page threshold at 40%. Also add an alert for sustained SM% > 90% over 10m (warn at 80%).

alex: nice — can you add the exact alert rule text or a pointer to the alert file? want to include in the handoff note.

irene: yup, gist -> https://gist.github.com/irene/kv-alerts-suggestion (short rules). excerpt: 
```
- alert: KVHitLow
  expr: sum(kv_cache_hits{pool="pool-42"}) / sum(kv_cache_lookups{pool="pool-42"}) < 0.55
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
- alert: KVHitPage
  expr: sum(kv_cache_hits{pool="pool-42"}) / sum(kv_cache_lookups{pool="pool-42"}) < 0.4
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
```

maya: panel shortlinks (so folks can embed in the runbook):
- SM%: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d-solo/gpu/SM-util?panelId=21&orgId=1&var-pool=pool-42
- KV hit: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d-solo/gpu/KV-hit?panelId=37&orgId=1&var-pool=pool-42
- Mem: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d-solo/gpu/Memory?panelId=12&orgId=1&var-pool=pool-42

chen: for traces, use the call-id from the failing request(s) — example trace for 02:14:33 is at: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/abcd-3344 (filter by pool and canary tag). shows a few repeated small model reloads due to cache churn.

sam: ops note — if KV hit stays low we should try increasing per-request batch_size target from 8 -> 12 on canary for 1 hour to see if throughput improves. low-risk experiment and easy rollback.

alex: thanks. can someone drop the canary tag + the commit sha so I can paste them in the handoff?

obs-bot: deploy bot: canary deploy completed by @maya — service/runtime v1.8.3-canary (sha: b7f3a2d) at 2412300000 :white_check_mark:

maya: sha above is correct. i also uploaded a quick snapshot csv to the runbook: https://internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/pool-42/snapshots/2412345678-snapshot.csv

irene: i'll open a PR for the alert changes (targeting staging) and tag @oncall for verification. put me down as owner for the alert tweak.

alex: perfect. last ask — if anyone has a one-line recommended remediation for the handoff (so oncall knows the first step), add it here. i'll compile.

chen: one-liner: "check KV hit panel, if <50% try increasing batch_size on canary to 12 and monitor evictions; rollback if memory evictions increase >5/min." :memo:

sam: +1 to that. also: if SM% > 92% across GPUs, scale up by +1 instance for the pool (manual or via capacity API). :thumbsup:

alex: awesome — thanks all. i'll paste this into the handoff note and close the loop. :pray:
